items.statement: Segmental difference in ATS insulates from large HFCs entering near-prime/affordable; no competitive pressure on target audience
items.quote: The way I look at the customer segment that we operate in, is primarily very different in ATS from what the larger NBFCs or HFCs look at. Hence, that clear segmental difference, fundamentally for me, as we progress ahead, does not put competitive pressure from these entities to my target audience.

items.statement: PLR not changed after repo hike; ALCO reviews monthly; incremental lending rates support yield on fresh disbursements
items.quote: No, not currently. We are examining it, and as and when we feel the need of a PLR change, we will make it happen.

items.statement: Liquidity ample: cash/CC limits ₹19.6 bn + unavailed sanctions ₹3 bn as of Sep 2026
items.quote: As of 30th Sep 2026, we maintained ample liquidity, including cash and cash equivalents and un -availed CC limits of Rs. 19.6 billion and documented un-availed sanctions of Rs. 3 billion.

items.statement: Q2FY27 borrowings ₹16.79 bn at 7.66%; total outstanding ₹216 bn; 30% repo-linked, rest MCLR/fixed; ALM positive
items.quote: We continued to borrow judiciously, raising around Rs. 16.79 bn at competitive rate at 7.66% for Q2FY27. As of 30th Sep 2026, total outstanding borrowings stood at Rs. 216 billion.

items.statement: 1+ DPD 3.81% (-18 bps YoY); Gross Stage 3 1.11% (-13 bps YoY); Net Stage 3 0.70% (-16 bps YoY); credit cost 24 bps H1FY27
items.quote: Our 1+ DPD improved by 18 bps YoY to 3.81% in Q2 FY27, remaining comfortably below 5%. Gross Stage 3 improved by 13 bps YoY to 1.11%, while Net Stage 3 improved by 16 bps YoY to 0.70%.

items.statement: Headcount down ~150 due to right-sizing and churn; not cutting people; investing in team; ESOP rolled out to ~200 employees
items.quote: We are not cutting down on people. We are making sure that every resource deployed is rightfully produced for the organization.

items.statement: Incentive policy revamped: starts from first disbursement, graded slabs, encourages direct sourcing within 40-50 km catchment
items.quote: The incentive structure starts from the first disbursement. Obviously, it has gradations and slabs as we move upwards.

items.statement: ROA 3.28% Q2FY27 (+9 bps QoQ); ROE 13.63% (+28 bps QoQ); CRAR 43.77%
items.quote: Our RoA expanded of 9 bps QoQ to 3.28% and RoE improved of 28 bps QoQ to 13.63% in Q2FY27.

items.statement: No asset quality hiccups expected from drought; minimal exposure to pure agri-income; Maharashtra concentration low
items.quote: No, I do not see Aavas having any hiccups on asset quality at all. On the drought situation, especially the point that you mentioned on Maharashtra, we are largely centric around Pune and some of the Marathwada districts like Latur, etc. Our concentration i s very minimal

items.statement: Insurance regulation from Apr 2027 may hit ~4% of PBT; confident to offset via higher attachment rates and risk-adjusted fee/yield levers
items.quote: Roughly about 50% of what one stands to lose mathematically because of the regulation coming in from 1st of April next year, we are very confident of pulling that through by making sure that our attachment percentages come in line with what competition is.

items.statement: Technology (SFDC, BRE, rule engines) driving productivity, pricing granularity, top-up loan automation, supervisor efficiency
items.quote: Today, we are running business rule engines which give out ranges for a transaction based on three or four facets. It is not a singular combination.

items.statement: Mutual fund quarterly average AUM was Rs. 4.02 lakh crores in Q2 FY27, up from Rs. 3.93 lakh crores in Q1 FY27, with market share of 4.61%
items.quote: Our mutual fund quarterly average AUM for quarter two of FY '27 stood at Rs. 4.02 lakh crores, compared with Rs. 3.93 lakh crores in quarter one of FY '27, representing a market share of 4.61%.

items.statement: Total group AUM stood at Rs. 16.28 lakh crores as of September 30, 2026
items.quote: Our total group AUM stood at Rs. 16.28 lakh crores as of September 30th, 2026.

items.statement: SIP AUM was Rs. 45,572 crores as of September 30, 2026, broadly stable vs Rs. 45,595 crores in June 2026
items.quote: Our SIP AUM stood at Rs. 45,572 crores as of September 30, 2026, broadly stable as compared with Rs. 45,595 crores in June of '26.

items.statement: Gross SIP inflows were Rs. 2,583 crores in Q2 FY27 and Rs. 5,085 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: The gross SIP inflows were Rs. 2,583 crores during this quarter and Rs. 5,085 crores during the half year of FY '27.

items.statement: Registered 5.96 lakh new SIPs in Q2 FY27, 87% sourced through digital channels
items.quote: Furthermore, we registered 5.96 lakh new SIPs during quarter two of FY '27, of which 87% were sourced through digital channels.

items.statement: Live folio base stood at 1.47 crores in Q2 FY27, added 3.6 lakh new investors in Q2 and 6.12 lakh in H1 FY27
items.quote: In quarter two of FY '27, our live folio base stood at 1.47 crores, and we added 3.6 lakh new investors as identified by their PAN. During the half year, w e added 6.12 lakh

items.statement: UTI Mutual Fund's share of industry's new SIP registration by volume was 4.08% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: UTI Mutual Fund's share of industry's new SIP registration by volume stood at 4.08% in quarter two.

items.statement: Net sales in Q2 FY27 were close to Rs. 5,720 crores; average AUM growth was around Rs. 10,000 crores
items.quote: It's close to around Rs. 10,000 crores of average AUM growth rate, and almost around Rs. 5,720 crores is from net sales.

items.statement: UTI Pension Fund AUM grew 10.97% YoY to Rs. 4.32 lakh crores as of September 30, 2026, managing 24.01% of NPS industry AUM
items.quote: UTI Pension Fund has recorded a year-on-year growth of approximately 10.97% in its AUM, reaching approximately Rs. 4.32 lakh crores as on 30th September 2026, as compared to Rs. 3.89 lakh crores as on 30th September 2025. It currently manages approximately 24.01% of the NPS industry's AUM.

items.statement: UTI International AUM was USD 1.67 billion (approx Rs. 16,063 crores) as of September 30, 2026
items.quote: UTI International, which represents our international business, has an AUM of US D1.67 billion, which is approximately Rs. 16,063 crores as on 30th September 2026.

items.statement: UTI Alternatives AUM grew 52% YoY to Rs. 4,045 crores as of September 2026
items.quote: UTI Alternatives' AUM has grown to approximately Rs. 4,045 crores, up 52% from Rs. 2,669 crores as on September of 2025.

items.statement: UTI SDOF IV crossed Rs. 1,000 crores milestone, AUM at Rs. 1,131 crores, fund size planned at Rs. 1,500 crores with greenshoe of Rs. 500 crores
items.quote: UTI SDOF IV has crossed the Rs. 1,000 crores milestone. Launched in quarter three of FY26 as the fourth fund in our SDOF series, the fund is planned as a Rs. 1,500 crores with a greenshoe option of Rs. 500 crores. It already has reached an AUM of Rs. 1,131 crores and is currently in raising and investing stage.

items.statement: Employee cost guidance maintained at Rs. 95 crores per quarter standalone and Rs. 130 crores per quarter consolidated for full financial year
items.value: 95 crores per quarter standalone, 130 crores per quarter consolidated
items.quote: As far as our overall guidance number for the employee cost is, that we are maintaining that for the standalone, it is close to around Rs. 95 crores per quarter, and for the consolidated, it is close to around Rs. 130 crores per quarter. We are maintaining that guidance number for the full financial year as well.

items.statement: Board policy to distribute 90-95% of profit as dividend; no plans for special dividend or incremental cash distribution
items.quote: So as of now, the board-level decision is that most of whatever the profit that we are generating, we will be distributing closer to 90 - 95% of that profit will be distributed as dividend. That dividend aggressive policy that we have continued over the last three to four years, and that should continue.

items.statement: Will launch UTI Classif Hybrid Long Short Fund in Q3 FY27 under SIF initiative
items.quote: We have received SEBI approval for our Specialised Investment Fund - SIF initiative and will be launching the UTI Classif Hybrid Long Short Fund in quarter three of FY27.

items.statement: UTI International to launch two new funds by end of Q3 or Q4 FY27
items.quote: We are launching a few products by the end of quarter three and quarter four. Hopefully, that should provide some traction of AUM and revenue growth in UTI International. But definitely, you will hear, either by the end of quarter three or quarter four, there are two new fund launches on the UTI International side.

items.statement: Consolidated core revenue from sale of services was Rs. 398 crores in Q2 FY27, up 2% YoY and 5% QoQ; core PAT was Rs. 131 crores, up 22% YoY and 2% QoQ
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the core income, i.e. the sale of service amounted to Rs. 398 crores, up by 2% Y-o-Y and 5% Q-o-Q. The core profit after tax for the quarter is Rs. 131 crores, up by 22% Y-o-Y and 2% Q-o-Q.

items.statement: Consolidated H1 FY27 core revenue Rs. 777 crores, up 1% YoY; core PAT Rs. 263 crores, up 15% YoY
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the core income amounted to Rs. 777 crores, up by 1% Y-o-Y. The core profit after tax for H1 FY27 is Rs. 263 crores, up by 15% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Segment yields: equity/hybrid ~73-74 bps, ETF/index ~8 bps, cash/arbitrage ~11 bps, fixed income ~20-21 bps
items.value: 73-74 bps equity, 8 bps ETF, 11 bps cash, 20-21 bps fixed income
items.quote: Yes. So, equity is roughly at around 73 -74 basis points, equity and hybrid fund. ETF and index fund will be around 8 basis points, cash and arbitrage 11, and fixed income fund is around 20-21 basis points.

items.statement: Weighted average yield flat at ~31 bps; marginal repricing impact from SEBI TER to BER changes passed to intermediaries
items.quote: I don't see any sequential increase in the yield number. The yield numbers are more or less, at a weighted average level, flat at around 31 basis points. Marginal could be there because of the repricing part.

items.statement: Equity-oriented schemes attracted Rs. 92,333 crores in Q2 FY27 industry-wide; monthly SIP contribution hit record Rs. 32,490 crores in September 2026
items.quote: Equity-oriented schemes attracted Rs. 92,333 crores in quarter two of FY '27, taking the first half FY '27 inflows to Rs. 1.83 lakh crores. In September '26, the equity inflows stood at Rs. 38,307 crores, while the monthly SIP contribution reached a record Rs. 32,490 crores.

items.statement: Small and mid-cap funds accounted for 44% of September equity inflows; flexi-cap, multi-cap, large & mid-cap, large-cap accounted for 41%
items.quote: Small and mid -cap funds accounted for 44% of September's equity inflows, while flexi -cap, multi -cap, large and mid -cap, and large -cap funds accounted another 41%.

items.statement: Equity-oriented assets 72% of average mutual fund AUM in Q2 FY27 vs ~70% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Equity-oriented assets across active and passive strategies accounted for 72% of our average mutual fund AUM, compared with approximately 70% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Launched UTI Balanced Hybrid Fund and four passive products linked to Nifty 500 and BSE India Sector Leaders indices in Q2 FY27
items.quote: During quarter two of FY27, we launched the UTI Balanced Hybrid Fund and four passive products linked to the Nifty 500 and BSE India Sector Leaders indices.

items.statement: SIP book concentration: Flexi-Cap 20.3%, sectoral/thematic 16%, Mid-Cap 15%, Large & Mid-Cap 12.7% of equity SIP inflows
items.quote: Flexi-Cap remains one of the largest, you know, contributor to the SIP book. So, nearly 20% of our inflows are coming still in Flexi-Cap, and that has remained broadly at around the same level last year from last year also. Last year it was about 19.3%, now it is about 20.3%. So, apart from that, we have funds like the sectoral and thematic funds which are contributing 16%, the Mid-Cap also contri

items.statement: Redemptions in equity coming from banks, national distributors, and to smaller extent MFDs and direct channel
items.quote: From a c hannel-wise perspective, we are seeing, you know, on the equity side redemptions are coming from banks as well as from the national distributors. There are some redemptions which are also seen from the MFDs, but banks, you know, and national distributors, we are seeing a higher amount of redemption on the equity side

items.statement: Fintech partners facilitated ~1 lakh transactions in Q2 FY27, contributed 67% of new investor acquisitions
items.quote: Our fintech partners facilitated approximate ly 1 lakh transactions during the quarter two of FY27 and these partners have contributed 67% of the new investor acquisitions.

items.statement: SIP closure rate ~70% vs industry ~80%, indicating better stickiness
items.quote: And even if you look at our closure rate of SIPs in the last quarter, while industry was trending at around 80%, our SIP closure book was around 70%. So, we are better off than industry in terms of SIP closure.

items.statement: Process optimisation generated ~Rs. 4.22 crores savings; automation reducing manual intervention
items.quote: Process optimisation generated approximately Rs. 4.22 crores in savings, while automation is reducing manual intervention.

items.statement: Delivered 10,690 training hours to sales team up to September 2026; strengthening performance management and critical talent retention
items.quote: We continue to invest in the organisational capability, with 10,690 training hours delivered to the sales team up to September of '26, while strengthening performance management and identifying critical talent for development and retention.

items.statement: Industry quarterly average AUM rose to Rs. 87.2 lakh crores in Q2 FY27 from Rs. 83.1 lakh crores in Q1 FY27; ETFs net inflows Rs. 15,501 crores in September 2026
items.quote: Industry quarterly average AUM rose to Rs. 87.2 lakh crores from Rs. 83.1 lakh crores in quarter one of FY '27, with ETFs recording net inflows of Rs. 15,501 crores in September '26.

items.statement: Industry SIP AUM at Rs. 17.86 lakh crores as of September 2026
items.quote: the SIP AUM being at Rs. 17.86 lakh crores for industry.

items.statement: Flexi-Cap fund remains a challenge with large outflows, though performance improved to first quartile in last three months
items.quote: As we mentioned earlier, Flexi-Cap remains still the challenge for us. While we have seen some inflows in Flexi-Cap, there have been large outflows also in the fund, and that remains a fund which we are focusing on. However, if you look at the last three months' performance, we are seeing that the fund performance has shown significant improvement, and now the Flexi-Cap fund is in the first quarti

items.statement: Management maintains full-year EBITDA guidance of INR750-800 crore and expects to be closer to the upper end given strong H1 performance.
items.quote: I think we are sticking to our guidance. In fact, we think we should given the strong performance in the first half of the year, we should hopefully be closer to the upper end of the guidance we have given for the year.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals portfolio targeted to grow at 20-25% year-on-year on a multi-year CAGR basis.
items.quote: But at an overall level, our aspiration is to continue to grow our specialty chemical portfolio at 20% to 25% year on year on a multi-year CAGR basis.

items.statement: Annual capex guidance maintained at INR400-500 crore, with Gajraula multipurpose plant commissioning in next few months.
items.quote: We will be investing at least INR400 crore to INR500 crore every year as we announced a couple of years back in our investor presentation also.

items.statement: CDMO pipeline peak potential near INR2,000 crore including large contract; ex-large contract peak potential INR1,500 crore+ with one-third expected this fiscal year.
items.quote: On the back of some of the incremental opportunities that we have secured, that full potential along with the big contract is close to INR2,000 crore, but even if I keep the big contract aside, we still have a big pipeline which I mentioned in my opening remarks also, with the peak potential of almost INR1,500 crore plus and at least one third of that we will we will clock in in in this year, in t

items.statement: Signed agreement to acquire 40% stake in Zettaone Technologies for INR189 crore; shareholders agreement to be concluded soon.
items.quote: I am delighted to share that we have recently signed an agreement to acquire 40% stake in Zettaone with an investment of INR189 crore.

items.statement: European competitor plant closures in acetic anhydride expected to strengthen demand and pricing from early next calendar year, viewed as multi-year opportunity.
items.quote: Regarding your question on the plant closure in Europe, it is a very recent development and things are still playing out on the ground. So, we expect some uplift starting to happen only from early part of next calendar year.

items.statement: Investments made over last 3-3.5 years expected to reach average 70%+ utilization by end of FY27, driving need for new multipurpose plants.
items.quote: Whatever investments we made in the last three, three and a half years, a lot of them will start reaching average 70% plus utilization levels by end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Consumer segment (personal care) grew to 7% of portfolio driven by vitamin B3 personal grade ramp-up and CDMO opportunities; targeting double digits within few quarters.
items.quote: I think one of the big reasons is as I think I have communicated in the past, we have been focusing in a big way on the personal care segment and while we already have vitamin B3 personal grade which has ramped up very quickly in recent months, we also have a few other products and a CDMO kind of opportunities where we have started to serve the customers.

items.statement: Vitamin B3 pricing softened in last few weeks, may linger into Q3; pyridine base pricing under pressure; most other segments holding prices.
items.quote: I think by and large most segments are holding up the price. So I am hoping there should not be any negative impact except for maybe vitamin B3 where we have seen some decline in the last few weeks which may linger into Q3.

items.statement: Zettaone standalone business grew 60-70% this year; market growing 35-40% annually; semiconductor funnel increased ~30% in recent months due to joint go-to-market efforts.
items.quote: In the last few years, the business has doubled and even this year, we are hoping it will grow at least 60% 70% and possibly even more.

items.statement: Large CDMO contract future volumes under discussion with multiple scenarios; visibility expected within few weeks; take-or-pay receivable risk fully protected per agreement.
items.quote: We are very close to concluding what the way forward would be and as soon as we have the visibility, we will be able to disclose that to all of you, hopefully within next few weeks.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals EBITDA margin at 25% in Q2 driven by improved pricing in value-added fine chemicals and CDMO portfolio.
items.quote: We delivered EBITDA of INR140 crore, translating into a strong EBITDA margin of 25%, driven by improved pricing across our value-added fine chemicals and CDMO portfolio.

items.statement: Confirmed CDMO molecule pipeline at 25+ with peak revenue potential INR1,500 crore+; adding ~25 molecules per year from 100+ funnel.
items.quote: Overall, we have 25 plus confirmed molecules in our pipeline, which are expected to drive our future growth in coming years.

items.statement: Input and utility costs partially offset improved acetyls pricing; chemical intermediates saw higher input costs from elevated crude prices.
items.quote: However, input and utility costs during the quarter partially offset the benefits of improved pricing.

items.statement: Acetyls volumes stable with pharma crude prices supporting improved realization; acetic anhydride healthy sequential volume growth from resilient pharma demand and Europe market share gains.
items.quote: Acetic anhydride delivered healthy sequential volume growth supported by resilient pharma demand and market share gains in Europe while maintaining a stable domestic market position.

items.statement: Revenue from stationary engine segment for data centers to reach $100 million peak by FY30, with 30% by FY28 and 50% by FY29
items.quote: FY'30, we will reach the run rate at least by Q3 or Q4 for that $100 million. 30% by FY'28 is what we feel, 50% by FY'29.

items.statement: Committed to 15% CAGR growth in real terms on a large base
items.quote: we have committed a 15% CAGR. Of course, some years we will grow much more than that. In the real terms not adjusted for inflation is what we say that we will be growing at 15%.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA target of 1.7-1.8x on consolidated basis for the year
items.quote: overall I think we will be at 1.7-1.8 net debt to EBITDA on a consolidated basis for the year.

items.statement: Inflection point at Rs 1,850 crores EBITDA next year, after which company will be self-sufficient for capex funding
items.quote: the inflection point for us is around Rs. 1,850 crores sort of EBITDA which we wi ll reach next year. After that we will be able to be self - sufficient for funding our CAPEX as well as the maintenance CAPEX

items.statement: Q3 capex expected at Rs 500-600 crores on consolidated level; Q4 capex to be minimal as long-term projects pushed to subsequent years
items.quote: Q3 on a console level will be between Rs. 500 crores-Rs. 600 crore on the CAPEX.

items.statement: German subsidiary machine shop investment very small, around Rs 20-30 crores; no major foreign capex or acquisitions planned
items.quote: maybe 20, 30 crores on a couple of machines there, so that we can support the foundry and reduce the working capital intent.

items.statement: Alloy wheel business at around 70% utilization in past couple of months
items.quote: Sir, we are at around 70% sort of current utilization level in the past couple of months, I would say.

items.statement: DR Axion Plant-2 started trial production with strong order book; Sunbeam transformation underway with Q3/Q4 expected to be better
items.quote: The DR Axion Plant-2 has started at least trial production I would say and the order book is also strong there. Sunbeam has gone through a very good transformation and we are in close contact with the customers on the way forward. Q3 and Q4 will be looking better for Sunbeam.

items.statement: Aluminum margin decline to 6.5% EBIT margin temporary; expects recovery after price correction discussions with customers in next two quarters
items.quote: Yes, we have seen some corrections of the margins in Aluminum that is not a correction, it is a temporary correction. We had increased our inventory because of the shortage of raw material and also the prices which were increasing dropped suddenly so we had an impact of that. So, with the price increase what we are negotiating with the customer or correction or compensation for the Aluminum price

items.statement: Price rationalization needed across legacy products due to sharp rise in manpower, energy and capital goods costs; reset magnitude 6-7% to 15-20% on gross margin/value addition portion
items.quote: It may vary, but anywhere between 6% -7% all the way to 15% -20% will be there depending on the commodity, the product and the time of the order. This is not on the top line, but on the gross margin or the value addition portion.

items.statement: Sunbeam exiting low-margin businesses; top line may reduce but absolute margins will improve as some products were negative at EBITDA level
items.quote: our top line may reduce, but our absolute margins will improve because some of them are negative on the EBITDA itself in general. There's no point in trying to reset those prices. So, with that, the P&L will be very healthy.

items.statement: Stationary engine order book around $100 million for data centers; inquiries and order push for next level of capacity quite strong
items.quote: The revenues will start from FY'29 and go into FY'30 where we will peak at around $100 million and the next level of peak we are expecting in the enquiries and order push is quite strong.

items.statement: Aluminum order pipeline long for order wins; new plants ramping up with operating leverage to improve in two quarters
items.quote: On the Aluminum, the pipeline is quite long for the whatever order wins we have. There are some headwinds on the new plants where we have to put in the working capital in and we have to start up the plants which is also happening as a suboptimum as of now. So, the operating leverage on those plants will take another two quarters to get into a profitable situation.

items.statement: India becoming manufacturing hub for powertrain exports to underdeveloped markets, South America, Africa, Asia; exports of tractors, two-wheelers, construction equipment increasing
items.quote: exports out of India as a product or an aggregate will continue to grow. So, there is opportunity for all tier 1, tier 2 suppliers like craftsman for on the growth strategy.

items.statement: Aluminum price spike and drop caused inventory impact; negotiating compensation with customers for past and future corrections
items.quote: We had increased our inventory because of the shortage of raw material and also the prices which were increasing dropped suddenly so we had an impact of that. So, with the price increase what we are negotiating with the customer or correction or compensation for the Aluminum price correction also which will play out in the coming two quarters.

items.statement: Gross debt increased due to working capital ballooning from significant top-line growth, GST credit buildup, pipeline inventory, and safety stock; safety stock to dilute in coming quarter
items.quote: Our top line growth is quite significant. So, working capital has ballooned and also the other say GST credit has ballooned and some of the pipeline we have added more lines or more plants. So, that pipeline inventory is yet to materialize into revenue on the matter. So, yes, and we are also carrying some safety stock of material which now will get diluted in the coming quarter.

items.statement: Broad-basing Aluminum components beyond legacy parts; seeing opportunities in EV and wider OEM product offerings
items.quote: we are also broad basing on the new product on the Aluminum components, not only the legacy parts but I think there are more opportunities coming in not only on the EV but in general, the product offerings of the OEMs have become more wider.

items.statement: Being more selective on customers and products based on lifecycle and profitability; able to attract larger customers with more profitable products
items.quote: We are little more selective on the customers as well as the product looking at the lifecycle and profitability since we have now the base which is stronger and our ability to attract slightly larger customers with more profitable products for supply within India or outside India is better now.

items.statement: Multinational OEMs using India as export hub for aggregates; 1.5L and below gasoline powertrains and sub-150cc two-wheelers major export opportunities
items.quote: whatever can be manufactured in India is getting shifted to India and India is being used as an export hub for the aggregates also. So, 1.5 liter and below for the passenger vehicle, especially on the gasoline side, it makes a lot of sense for any OEM to get the powertrain out of India, exported out of India.

items.statement: Aluminum content per vehicle in India less than half of developed markets on ICE, maybe one-third; significant scope for growth on both ICE and EV platforms
items.quote: India has got one of the lowest Aluminum content per vehicle on the ICE also, and plus on the EV also, both. So, comparably, as a percentage of the vehicle weight on the ICE, we are less than half of the developed market, not even half, maybe one- third.

items.statement: Not a fan of investing outside India in big way due to associated risks; German subsidiary investment strategic and small; averse to foreign acquisitions
items.quote: I want to make one very clear statement is, we are not a fan of investing outside India in a big way because we understand the risks which are associated. This is a very strategic investment and we will keep it in that way.

items.statement: Commodity price risk on Aluminum; cannot get margin on increased Aluminum price; some moderation expected
items.quote: commodity price is a subject where we cannot get the increased Aluminum price, we cannot get a margin for that Aluminum also. So, we have to look at it that way. Some moderation will be there.

items.statement: Planning to close FY27 at ₹580-600 Cr top line and double PAT margin
items.quote: And, planning to close the financial year at, around ₹580 Cr to ₹600 Cr as a top line, and, double the PAT margin, EBITDA say ₹12.5 Cr for H1 result.

items.statement: Industry margins range 10-25%, sometimes 7-8%; company maintains margins even when freight rates rise
items.quote: What is the industry margin? 10tTo 25%, 15%, Sometimes it goes down to 7-8%, but yeah, that's roughly the… Ballpark range.

items.statement: Margins will increase quarter on quarter as infrastructure can handle double current business
items.quote: So, margin, bottom line, you will see increasing quarter on quarter and year on year, definitely.

items.statement: H1 FY27 shipments grew 56% to 674 and tonnage grew 32.84% to 744 tons
items.quote: You can see the growth in the number of shipments also from 430 shipments to 674 shipments the H1. And, tonnage also is increased. From 545 tons to 744 tons.

items.statement: E-commerce and courier growing multi-fold internationally; retail courier launched this month
items.quote: E-commerce and Courier is one of the products that is growing rapidly. The growth that you have seen in e-commerce and Courier in the last 10 years domestically, that same growth is happening internationally now.

items.statement: India air cargo target 10 million tons by 2030, nearly 2.7x current volume
items.quote: India's Ministry of Civilization has set a policy target of 10 million tons of air cargo by annually by 2030 . So it's almost 2.7 times its current volume.

items.statement: Building technology platform like MakeMyTrip for cargo; expected ready by end of year
items.quote: We're also look… looking at… our technology platform, wherein we are trying to do something like MakeMyTrip, but for cargo and courier. So, you know the platform is currently being built, but within a few months from now, I think it should be ready, hopefully by the end of the year.

items.statement: Current infrastructure can handle double the business volume
items.quote: Our costs remain the same, our infrastructure… current infrastructure can even do double the business that we are currently doing.

items.statement: Ocean freight is 70-80% of global trade; company plans to grow ocean freight for scale
items.quote: Currently, ocean freight is 70-80% of all global trade volumes, so that is where you know, we would like, like I said earlier, also, we would like to have some market share, or some big… so if we want to grow the company to a great extent, we are going to look at Ocean Freight.

items.statement: Top 3 with major airlines (Air India, Emirates, Qatar, Lufthansa); serve large supermarkets Lulu, Nesto via charters
items.quote: We feature amongst the top 10 in India, and we are among the number one, in the top 3 in most airlines out of India, like Air India, Emirates, Qatar, Lufthansa, and most airlines we feature among the top 3.

items.statement: Did 40-70 charters for large supermarkets; plan to broker charters directly via Dubai acquisition
